final_claim.narrative: Static reachability from 1006 to 1860 clearly exists: the 2-hop neighbourhood of 1006 (step_03) is dominated by hubs 14 and 45, whose neighbour sets include 153, 182, 274, 618, 958 and 1433 — six of the eleven distinct partners of 1860 (step_04). However, that is exactly the confound the task warns about: hub-mediated connectivity when time is ignored. The graph is sparse and near-simple (16325 events over 15767 distinct edges, repeat ratio 0.034, step_01), and both endpoints are low-activity nodes (1006: 9 events/9 partners; 1860: 11 events/11 partners, step_02), so any candidate relay path would rest on single, non-repeated contacts whose timestamps must each fall inside [18031, 56431] and be separated by no more than 600 units. None of the available tools returns event timestamps or per-edge times, so I could not verify ordering or the 600-unit inter-hop delay for any of the hub-mediated routes; the 600-unit constraint is tight relative to the ~100000-unit horizon, and hub edges are spread across it, so a static path is weak evidence for a temporal one. I therefore report insufficient rather than asserting a cascade that only aggregate connectivity supports.
